subject: Northbridge capacity playbook: Dedicated vs Private deployment
messages:
From: Joel Sanders <joel.sanders@northbridgehealth.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@northbridgehealth.com
Date: 2026-09-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sizing ask for regulated inference - initial request

Hi Laura,

We're kicking off scoping for the inference platform decision for a regulated imaging workflow. The workload will process de-identified imaging metadata and clinician notes; however, all logs and telemetry must be retained within our environment and meet our audit requirements. We need a capacity sketch and a comparison between: (A) Reserved/Dedicated capacity on Redwood's hosted platform with strict isolation controls, and (B) Private (customer-managed VPC or on-prem) deployment.

Initial constraints: expected steady-state 10 rps text-generation calls (50k tokens/min average), spiky peaks to 45 rps during daily batch windows, 1.5s target P95 latency for interactive workflows. KV cache hit expected ~55%. SLA required: 99.95 uptime, plus audit logs for token-level access.

Can your team produce a short playbook with: GPU fleet sizing (types & counts), expected latency/cost tradeoffs, timeline to availability, and a recommended rollout path (canary/dual-run)? Procurement would like ballpark recurring cost and any one-time engineering/setup fees. We can share a fuller workload CSV — attached is a trimmed profile.

Thanks,
Joel Sanders
Procurement Manager
Northbridge Health

Attachment: nb_workload_profile.csv (3 KB)

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-06T10:34:00-07:00
Subject: Northbridge capacity playbook (Dedicated vs Private) — recommendation and model attached

Joel / Laura — attached is a concise playbook and the capacity model (xlsx). Summary points below.

Executive summary:
- Recommendation: Start with Redwood Dedicated Reserved capacity (VPC-isolated, customer-managed KMS option) for fastest time-to-production and predictable economics; evaluate a Private deployment for long-term isolation if additional legal controls or on-prem hardware requirements emerge.
- Rationale: Dedicated gives you SLA-backed throughput, easier operational handoff, and faster delivery (6–8 weeks). Private requires additional NRE for deployment automation and on-prem validation (12–16 weeks + licensed infra).

Sizing and performance assumptions (based on your CSV):
- Workload: interactive chat + nightly batch spikes. Avg token rate: 50k tokens/min; peak burst to 225k tokens/min. KV cache hit: 55%.
- Target: P95 <= 1.5s for interactive flows.

Scenario A — Redwood Dedicated (recommended initial):
- Suggested runtime: heterogeneous fleet using H100-80GB for peak model replicas; A100-80GB for baseline cost-optimized replicas.
- Starting capacity: 6 x H100-80GB (hot replicas) + 10 x A100-80GB (warm replicas) behind smart routing. Estimated sustained headroom for 10 rps steady, headroom to 45 rps with autoscale to burst pool.
- Expected P95 latency: 0.9–1.4s (depending on model variant).
- Monthly recurring cost (est.): $145,000–$170,000 (committed reserved pricing).
- Service-level: 99.95 SLA, automated fallbacks to smaller quantized model with graceful degradation.
- Time to provision: 6–8 weeks (contract, capacity reservation, canary).
- Pros: linear support model, no on-prem ops, faster security evidence handoff (SOC2 + per-tenant audit logs).
- Cons: still co-located in Redwood-managed DCs; requires strict tenancy and KMS integration for your audit model.

Scenario B — Private (VPC / customer-managed environment):
- Suggested runtime: 6–8 x H100-80GB (full private fleet), additional 2 x H100 as hot spares for HA.
- Expected P95 latency: 0.8–1.3s (network/infra dependent).
- Recurring cost (incl. support & managed upgrades): $165,000–$210,000/month plus an initial engineering/onboarding fee: $85,000–$120,000 (one-time).
- Time to provision: 12–16 weeks (provisioning, secure networking, on-site validation).
- Pros: full control for logs/retention, fits strict legal/perimeter controls; easier to demonstrate air-gapped proofs if later needed.
- Cons: higher one-time cost, ongoing patching/resilience responsibility, longer time to scale quickly for spikes.

Key trade-offs and mitigations:
- Audit logs: both options support token-level audit exports; Private gives you immediate custody, Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS + privileged access controls.
- Scaling: Dedicated + reserved capacity + burst autoscaling is best for unpredictable spikes with predictable cost; Private requires capacity buffer or burst-burst plan with procurement lead time.
- Rollout recommendation: staged canary (5% traffic) on Dedicated, run parallel traffic for 2 weeks, then expand to 50% while retaining fallbacks to quantized models. If legal requires full segregation, plan Private migration in Phase 2.

Attachments: capacity_model_northbridge_20260904.xlsx, deployment_tradeoffs_summary.pdf, soc2_evidence_redwood.pdf

Action items (mutual action plan):
- Redwood to deliver SOW & committed pricing for Dedicated by 2026-09-08. (Laura)
- Northbridge to confirm KMS approach and sign NDA for SOC2 artifacts access by 2026-09-10. (Joel)
- Technical pilot can commence within 2 business days of contract signature. (Marissa & Karthik)

Let me know if you want the model re-run for different reservation terms (12 vs 36 months) or different quantization profiles.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
